resources.string: Join the adapter\'s Wi-Fi network first, then enter its address (host:port).
Bluetooth permission is needed to talk to the adapter
MPS Diag needs permission to use Bluetooth (and, on Android 11 and older, location for scanning).
Plug the adapter into the OBD socket and turn the ignition ON, then tap your adapter below. Not listed? Tap Scan.
Scanning for adapters… keep the adapter plugged in and powered.
No paired devices. Tap Scan, or pair the adapter in Bluetooth settings (PIN usually 1234 or 0000).

%1$s\n\nCheck that: the adapter is plugged in and its light is on · it is not connected to another app or phone · it is paired (PIN 1234 or 0000) · for BLE adapters, don\'t pair in settings — just scan here.
Live data, forced regeneration, DPF replacement
This ECU does not support DPF regeneration or service resets.
VIN not reported · pick the engine when starting

The exhaust gets very hot (about 600 °C) during regeneration.

• Do it outdoors or in a well-ventilated area, away from people and anything flammable near the exhaust.
• If the engine warning light is on, read and fix fault codes first.
• Vehicle on level ground, selector in P / neutral with handbrake on.
• Engine running at idle, warmed up.

After you press Start, idle rises to about 1500–2000 rpm. It stops by itself after about 25 minutes, or when you press the accelerator. When it completes, the DPF light goes out.

On the 4N14 this regeneration is done while driving.

• Use it when the engine warning light and the DPF symbol are on.
• Start and warm the engine at idle, parked on level ground in P.
• Press Start: idle rises above 1000 rpm and the yellow DPF symbol confirms it started.
• Then drive in 3rd gear at 40 km/h or more and at least 2000 rpm (a bit more if it does not start). Expect 20–45 minutes.
• Stopping may interrupt it; it resumes if you drive off again within about 100 seconds.

Afterwards switch the ignition off and on and check the DPF symbol is gone. The exhaust is very hot when you stop — keep people and flammable things away.
The ECU accepted the request. Watch \"DPF regeneration operating\" and the time remaining below.
Run \"%1$s\"?\n\nOnly do this after the matching repair or part replacement. Ignition ON.

After an oil change on a 4N15 or 4N14 engine, if fault P252F (oil level too high / oil dilution) appears, reset the oil service here.\n\nIgnition ON, engine OFF. No forced DPF regeneration is needed afterwards.
Reset the oil dilution / oil change learning in the engine ECU?\n\nIgnition must be ON with the engine OFF. Only do this right after an oil change.
Choose a module and read its fault codes. Ignition ON.
Clear all fault codes in \"%1$s\"?\n\nIgnition ON, engine OFF. Codes for faults that are still present will come back.
Fault codes cleared in %1$s. Reading again…
Could not clear codes in %1$s: %2$s\nThe fault may still be present — fix it and try again.
